annotationRationale: The central task is converting uniform continuous probability into a covered-area ratio while checking overlap and boundary effects. Circle area, square area, and decimal rounding support both routes; counting lattice points is specific to the second method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Under the usual continuous uniform area model, the probability is πd² for 0≤d≤1/2. Since coverage at 1/2 is π/4>1/2, the required radius is d=1/√(2π)≈0.3989, rounding to B, 0.4. The stem, choices and key agree; no figure is required.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Independently verified and retained both shared methods from 2020_AMC_10A_Q16: unit-square-areas and count-boundary-disk-pieces. They provide useful local-cell and whole-square boundary arguments. The AoPS estimation variants are equivalent numerical finishes and need no separate route.
review.annotationCheck: Uniform geometric probability is the correct assessed concept. Circle area, square area and rounding are appropriate support concepts. Lattice counting is correctly confined to the boundary-counting method.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For r≤1/2, each cell contains four quarter-disks with disjoint interiors and total area πr². Noncorner lattice points cannot contribute. Summing over 2020² cells gives probability πr², including boundary cells. The radius restriction, positive square root and rounding are correct.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately reuses 2020_AMC_10A_Q16#unit-square-areas and retains both inherited AMC 10A LIVE and AoPS reference IDs. The current AMC 12A references support the same route. Project reuse and nonofficial third-party influence are honestly identified by source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The uniform sampling assumption, reduction to one cell, nonoverlap restriction and boundary treatment are explained sufficiently for independent reconstruction.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four immediate nodes match the written calculation. The exact geometric-probability node captures the central reasoning.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native-topic links for circle area, square area and decimal rounding fit. Geometric probability has no accepted CN link; this is a legitimate alignment gap.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The area and rounding strands of 7.G.B.4, the supplied rectangle-area standards and 5.NBT.A.4 fit. Circumference, G-GMD.A.1 formula derivations, perimeter and fractional-side tiling are not demonstrated. No accepted US link covers the central continuous probability concept.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The geometric-probability definition directly covers uniform area ratios, overlap and boundary checks. The three elementary support nodes are appropriate.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The disjoint categories contain (N−1)² interior centers, 4(N−1) side centers and four corners. Their disk weights sum to (N−1)²+2(N−1)+1=N². Outside centers contribute nothing for r≤1/2. The resulting probability πr² yields d≈0.3989 and B.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly retains 2020_AMC_10A_Q16#count-boundary-disk-pieces and its required inherited AoPS reference ID. The route matches AoPS Solution 7 and is properly labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The table entries, endpoint conventions and weighted total are explained. This method independently establishes the answer and handles the large square's boundary explicitly.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The lattice-counting node precisely captures the interior and boundary counts. Geometric probability, circle area, square area and rounding are all used.
